record.original_question: Consider a non-Hermitian $A ^n x n$ and suppose $Q ^n x k$ has orthonormal columns. We know that the Ritz values (eigenvalues of $Q*AQ$) are located in the numerical range, $W(A) = v*Av: |v |_2=1 $, a closed, convex subset of $ $ that contains the eigenvalues of $A$ (and, potentially, points far from these eigenvalues). What can be said (deterministically or probabalistically) about the distribution of the Ritz values across $W(A)$ for $1<k<n$? What if $Q$ is restricted to be a basis for a Krylov subspace? What if $Q$ is the basis for a random subspace?

evidence.quote: Consider a non-Hermitian $A\in\C^{n\times n}$ and suppose $Q\in\C^{n\times k}$ has orthonormal columns. We know that the Ritz values (eigenvalues of $Q^*AQ$) are located in the numerical range, $W(A) = \{v^*Av: \|v\|_2=1\}$, a closed, convex subset of $\C$ that contains the eigenvalues of $A$ (and, potentially, points far from these eigenvalues). \begin{itemize} \item What can be said (deterministically or probabalistically) about the distribution of the Ritz values across $W(A)$ for $1<k<n$? \item What if $Q$ is restricted to be a basis for a Krylov subspace? What if $Q$ is the basis for a random subspace? \end{itemize}

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be a (generally non-Hermitian) matrix, and let $Q \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times k}$ have orthonormal columns, with $1 < k < n$. The Ritz values of $A$ with respect to the column space of $Q$ are the eigenvalues of the compression $Q^* A Q \in \mathbb{C}^{k\times k}$. Let
$$W(A) = \{v^* A v : v \in \mathbb{C}^n,\ \|v\|_2 = 1\}$$
denote the numerical range of $A$, a closed convex subset of $\mathbb{C}$ that contains the spectrum of $A$ but may also contain points far from it. It is classical that every Ritz value lies in $W(A)$.

Provide a quantitative description, either deterministic or probabilistic, of how the $k$ Ritz values distribute themselves within $W(A)$. In particular, address the following three settings:

(a) The general case, where $Q$ is an arbitrary $n\times k$ matrix with orthonormal columns.

(b) The Krylov case, where the column space of $Q$ equals the Krylov subspace $\mathcal{K}_k(A,b) = \mathrm{span}\{b, Ab, A^2 b, \dots, A^{k-1} b\}$ for some starting vector $b \in \mathbb{C}^n$.

(c) The random case, where the column space of $Q$ is a uniformly distributed (Haar-random) $k$-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb{C}^n$.

Determine, in each setting, what can be proved about the empirical distribution of Ritz values in $W(A)$ as a function of $A$, $k$, and (where applicable) the starting vector $b$.
artifact.category_tag: Ritz value distribution for non-Hermitian matrices
artifact.status_search_result: The distribution of Ritz values inside the numerical range of a non-Hermitian matrix is broadly recognized as poorly understood beyond basic localization (Ritz values lie in W(A)). Existing work (e.g., Ritz value localization for non-Hermitian matrices by Carden–Embree, and recent work on estimating the numerical range with a Krylov subspace) provides partial bounds and estimates, but a full deterministic or probabilistic description—especially for general orthonormal Q, Krylov subspaces, and Haar-random subspaces—remains open.

status_evidence.title: Ritz Value Localization for Non-Hermitian Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Beyond the Hermitian case, our understanding remains surprisingly primitive... little has been said beyond the tautology that all Ritz values must fall within the numerical range.
status_evidence.claim: The non-Hermitian Ritz value distribution problem is largely open.

status_evidence.title: Estimating the Numerical Range with a Krylov Subspace
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the approximation quality of Krylov subspaces for estimating the numerical range, with bounds depending on matrix and Krylov subspace dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial results address the Krylov case but do not fully characterize Ritz value distribution.
